items.summary: Advance C13-AUTH-SCOPE-DIRECTION from planned with exact evidence
notes: The downward half needs discrimination rather than construction for authority and has no evidence at all for policy: src/authority/runtime.ts#TenantAuthorityRuntime and src/composition/authority.ts already resolve along the ordered Tenant-to-target path under C13-AUTH-DENY-PRECEDENCE and C13-AUTH-PATH-ORDER, while nothing asserts that declared PolicySet material — enforcement tiers, quotas, retention — resolves along that same path, so a host resolving policy per-Workspace only would satisfy every current test

items.summary: Advance C13-BLUEPRINT-CONVERGENCE from planned with exact evidence
notes: Nothing built today discriminates convergence from the idempotence C13-BLUEPRINT-REMATERIALIZE already verifies. Its selector proves re-applying one unchanged Blueprint reconciles to a semantic no-op, which is f(f(x)) = f(x) for one input; path-independence needs a differential harness that applies one Blueprint to a Scope by at least two admissible issue orders and from at least two different prior managed states, then asserts one identical Blueprint-managed record set once the pending set is empty. An implementation that reached the declared state only from an empty Scope must fail it

The pending set has to be carried by the reconciliation outcome rather than computed alongside it, so that converged is that set being empty rather than a separate report a host can get wrong. Verification requires the outcome type to hold the obligations and a mutation that states convergence while an obligation stands to break a cited test; a boolean flag set next to a nonempty obligation list satisfies the prose and must not satisfy the atom

Each of the four stated deferrals needs its own obligation-shape evidence — record, reason, and discharging condition all named: a reliance hold under C13-FACET-DEPENDENCY-ORDER, each draining Invocation item under C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-DRAIN, each unadmitted RouteReservation terminalized by a rejected RouteDelivery, and a Package retained under SPEC 5.2. No current test exercises any of them, and the Package case additionally has no coverage of the Session, tree-checkpoint, and Snapshot pin holders

The rejected-reconciliation clause is what stops converging from becoming an excuse, so it needs the strongest negative evidence: a divergence expressible as no pending obligation — a withdrawal set the host cannot compute, or a retired Slot declaration still holding an entry attributed to a retained Facet — must be refused at validation before package code loads, on the no-code-loaded terms C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD already tests, and must never be admitted and left pending

The managed-set scoping needs its own test because it is what makes the endpoint a function at all: an adopted manual edit must appear as a change to the Blueprint, and a host that marks an adopted record Blueprint-managed without a declaring Blueprint must be rejected. src/definition/materializer.ts#LocalMaterializer marks managed state but has no adoption path to discriminate

This rule's paragraph tightened the SPEC 9.3 retention condition from 'no Run references it' to the full SPEC 5.2 pin-holder set, so C13-BLUEPRINT-RUN-PINS carries anchored text whose Turn, Session, tree-checkpoint, and Snapshot cases its two selectors do not exercise. That atom was demoted from verified to implemented rather than left over-credited, and it now names the per-pin-holder retention tests it owes. This atom cannot be verified while the fourth deferral's discharging condition is under-covered by the neighbour that owns it

SPEC 9.3 previously deferred removing a pinned Package until 'no Run references it', while SPEC 5.2 keeps a Package release resolvable while any Run, Turn, Session, tree checkpoint, or Snapshot pins it; Session and Snapshot outlive a Run, so as written the clause licensed a removal 5.2 forbids. The discharge side needs the mirror evidence: removal must proceed once the last pin holder of any kind releases, so a host that never removes is not silently credited with satisfying a deferral rule

items.summary: Advance C13-CLOUDFLARE-ALARM-DURABILITY from implemented with exact evidence
notes: The corrected §10.4 rule bounds platform re-firing and requires the Actor to rebuild the alarm from the outbox on start. createCloudflareDurableObjectClass arms that rebuild under blockConcurrencyWhile, but no test named here exercises a start that recovers an alarm the platform stopped re-firing, and the live lane owes that scenario under ACQ-LIVE.

The platform exposes alarmInfo.retryCount and alarmInfo.isRetry (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/#alarm) and the adapter reads neither: durable-object.ts#alarm takes no parameter, so the object cannot tell how close the platform is to abandoning a schedule and cannot record it. Owed as evidence for the bounded-re-firing clause.

blockConcurrencyWhile is a documented whole-object stall that resets the object at thirty seconds and on any throw (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/state/#blockconcurrencywhile), and setAlarm inside a constructor is a documented hazard because the constructor runs before the alarm handler on wake (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/#setalarm). durable-object.ts calls a host-supplied repairAlarm inside blockConcurrencyWhile, which is both at once. It converges because the repair is derived from the outbox rather than an unconditional setAlarm, but nothing in the package bounds the host callback or records why the constructor may touch the alarm at all.

The fifteen-minute alarm wall-time cap (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/#wall-time-limits-by-invocation-type) and the CPU budget between network events (same page, footnote 4) are unmodelled: a sweep killed at either boundary is not a throw, so it reaches neither AlarmOutboxReconciler's retry path nor its floored re-arm. The resumption journal bounds the loss to one uncommitted step but nothing bounds the sweep itself.

items.summary: Advance C13-CLOUDFLARE-DEPLOYMENT-CONTINUITY from implemented with exact evidence
notes: Its prerequisite C13-CLOUDFLARE-ALARM-DURABILITY carries an open obligation, so continuity cannot rest on it yet.

The rollback direction is now stated in §10.4 and implemented: createCloudflareDurableObjectClass constructs an object whose applied schema this release cannot read and refuses each operation with schema.unreadable, leaving the durable state untouched. cloudflare/test/deployment-rollback.test.ts covers N to N+1 to N and back to N+1 on real SQLite, which closes the structural half of the obligation this atom carried.

Continuity across a rollout is not only schema continuity. Cloudflare documents that a request can reach a new Worker version and call a Durable Object still running the previous version for seconds to minutes (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/known-issues/#code-updates), that many exceptions leave a stub permanently broken, that errors carry .retryable and .overloaded properties, and that a retryable error should be retried with backoff on a freshly created stub while an overloaded one must not be retried at all (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/error-handling/). The adapter classifies none of this: grep for retryable and overloaded across cloudflare/src returns nothing, namespace.ts and placement.ts hand back raw stubs, and neither property is declared in the generated worker-configuration.d.ts, so reading them needs an explicit narrowing at the boundary that does not exist. The documented stub-lookup rate limit and the thousand-request-per-second soft limit reach the caller the same unclassified way. This is the most production-proven gap in the corpus and it has no §10 clause; the clause is owed before the code.

The bound is one per adapter, not one per §4.7 consumer. items.summary: Advance C13-CLOUDFLARE-STORAGE-LIMIT from implemented with exact evidence
notes: The named live case claims it stores a row at the declared limit, and its own comment says the seam is only correct if production accepts a row that large with overhead included, but it wrote SQL_BLOB_LIMIT_BYTES - 1_000 and exercised neither boundary. It now writes at the limit and owes a live run. The documented bound covers a string, BLOB or row while requireStorableBlob measures only the payload, so at-limit acceptance rests on workerd's undocumented SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH headroom rather than on anything Cloudflare promises.

SQLITE_FULL is documented as the failure a Durable Object at its ten-gigabyte storage limit returns for every write while reads and DELETEs keep working, and a storage operation that exceeds the platform's internal timeout is documented to reset the object (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/#what-happens-when-a-durable-object-exceeds-its-storage-limit, https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/observability/troubleshooting/). Neither is classified: CloudflareSqlite maps both to a generic protocol.invalid-state, so a full object is indistinguishable from a malformed statement and the documented drain-to-recover path cannot be taken.

Two further documented SQL bounds are unenforced: the hundred-kilobyte statement length and the hundred-bound-parameter cap (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/#sql-storage-limits). Nothing in the package approaches either today, and nothing prevents a host from doing so.

The two size seams in this package measure bytes the platform does not. requireStorableBlob measures the payload against a bound the documentation applies to the whole row, and the WebSocket attachment guard measures UTF-8 JSON bytes against a bound the platform applies to the structured clone (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/websockets/#websocketserializeattachment). Both approximations are stated in comments; neither is derived. A payload the storage seam accepts is also not bounded against the transport that has to carry it: a near-limit ViewDelta becomes roughly 2.7 MB of base64 in one frame, and the outbound frame ceiling is undocumented, so the delta can be unsendable to its own subscribers as an opaque socket failure.

The R2 content path buffers whole objects inside a 128 MB isolate — content-object.ts copies the payload on put and reads the entire body on get — with no size, key-length or metadata guard against R2's documented 1,024-byte key and 8,192-byte metadata bounds (https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/platform/limits/, https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#memory). §10.1 routes the ContentStore to R2 expressly for large content, so this is the one path where the memory limit rather than the storage limit is the binding constraint.

items.summary: Advance C13-CODEC-INCOMPATIBILITY-TOTAL from planned with exact evidence
notes: Neither half exists. src/core/codec.ts#RecordCodec stamps `{ kind, version: { major, minor }, payload }` on every encode and decides compatibility inside decode, one record at a time, so incompatibility is discovered by reading rather than from a declaration a reader reaches before any read. There is no record-set-level declaration to check and nowhere to check one: the codec is a per-record object held by each record class — RunCommit.codec, Environment.codec, PortExposure.codec and the rest — and no Actor declares the codec version of the records it owns

The totality half changes behaviour rather than only timing, and its conformance cases are the derivations this document already builds over whole record sets. A store whose incompatible rows are the ones a caller has not reached serves normally today, so reserved-minus-completed under C13-RUN-FRONTIER-COMPLETE, an ancestry walk under C13-RUN-ANCESTRY, and the settlement test under C13-RUN-SETTLED-DERIVED can each answer from the subset that decodes and return a wrong answer where a rejection would have returned none. Each of the three is owed as a case that rejects rather than answering short. Cross-wave ownership answered, since naming a foreign atom is not the same as owing its evidence: C13-RUN-FRONTIER-COMPLETE, C13-RUN-ANCESTRY and C13-RUN-SETTLED-DERIVED are W5 atoms over W5 records, and this row is W1. requireEvidenceOwner admits sourceSymbols only under the owning wave or W9, so a W1 row can never cite src/agents/runs symbols and must not try. The three derivation cases are therefore W5's to evidence under W5 rows once the record-set-level declaration exists — not this row's to cite and not this row's to block on. What this row owes is the substrate-neutral declaration and its total refusal at the W1 seam; what those three owe is that each rejects rather than answering short over a partially decodable set. Stated so a promoter reads three named atoms as the scope of the behaviour change rather than as evidence this row must produce

The recovery half needs both directions asserted, because a reader that refused by failing to construct would satisfy a rejection-only test. An incompatible declaration leaves every operation failing with the codec's typed error while the set stays addressable for inspection and export, the durable bytes are unchanged afterwards, and a reader that understands the declared version then serves the same set with no repair step

The Cloudflare profile already implements this rule for its own schema markers and is the working reference rather than a second mechanism: packages/agent-core-cloudflare/src/migration.ts raises the stable `schema.unreadable` code for an undeclared, corrupt, or duplicated marker, and the Durable Object class captures that one refusal at construction and raises it from fetch, alarm, and every socket entry point under C13-CLOUDFLARE-ROLLBACK-WINDOW. What is owed here is the substrate-level obligation that profile specialises, so a non-Cloudflare substrate owes the same property. Ownership answered, because this path was enumerated as a structural-ownership-blocker candidate: packages/agent-core-cloudflare/src/migration.ts is W8 while this row is W1, and it is named here as a working PRECEDENT and never as a required citation. items.summary: Advance C13-FACET-CANCELLATION-REACH from implemented with exact evidence
notes: The reachability conjunct is built and partly tested, so what remains here is narrower than construction: src/facets/runtime.ts#OperationContext declares a required `signal: AbortSignal`, and a Turn's cancellation reaches it through the scope signal TurnExecutor hands its executor, GatewayTurnInvocationPort's TurnGatewayScope, ComposedTurnGatewaySource.open calling operations(scope.signal), and the shared { signal, content } resources both DerivedDirectOperationContext and CanonicalBatchInvocationPort put on the handler's context. test/composition/mediation-pipeline.test.ts already discriminates the never-abort substitute over the concrete pipeline — 'the published mediation composition root runs each Operation under its own Turn's cancellation signal' asserts the handler's observed context signal is identically the Turn's signal and that an already-aborted Turn signal prevents dispatch with zero handler calls — but it carries no atom tag, so it is not yet conformance evidence for this row under scripts/quality/ledger.mjs's priority-evidence rule

What no test does is abort a Turn while an Operation handler is suspended and observe that handler's own context signal fire: the pipeline case aborts before invoke and then uses a controller it never aborts, and the only mid-execution abort observation in the suite is on a facet `start` hook's FacetLifecycleContext in test/operations/runtime.test.ts, not on an OperationContext. Availability at handler entry and observability during handler execution are different claims, and this rule makes the second one

The distinction this rule exists for is untested: an attempt whose wait the host abandoned must record `indeterminate` while an attempt whose handler observed its context cancellation must record `aborted` under C13-RECEIPT-FAILURE-KIND, and a mutation substituting a never-abort sentinel for the context signal must collapse the second case into the first rather than leaving both green

Propagation past the seam has no enforcement point at all. Nothing requires a handler that awaits further asynchronous work under its own invocation's lifetime to pass its context cancellation on, and nothing keeps a bound it derives linked to the cancellation it derived from. Closure needs a profile handler that delegates — §11.2 Shell is the sharpest, since P11-SHELL-CANCELLATION already asserts prompt cancellation — proving the abort reaches the side-effect owner, that awaited work reaches quiescence, and that a handler deriving a narrower deadline still aborts when the upstream cancellation fires

The schema exclusion is unchecked: OperationDescriptor.input accepts any JsonSchema, so nothing today refuses a declared input property that purports to carry cancellation, and nothing proves a handler cannot be reachable only through such a field. Verification requires the install-time manifest validation to refuse it, not the first invocation to fail on it

The durable-record boundary is satisfied by construction rather than by assertion, which is the direction a regression would come from: the ContentStore seam and the §8.5 command dispatcher take no signal, so an added one would silently widen this atom into the requirement it explicitly is not. A conformance assertion that those two seams stay cancellation-free is what keeps this rule from being read as requiring cancellation everywhere

Promotion to verified is blocked across a fragment boundary and the blocker is a true dependency rather than a bookkeeping accident: this row names C13-RECEIPT-FAILURE-KIND, which is W6's in invocations-audit.json and planned, so ledger.mjs's verified-status monotonicity rejects a verified row here until §7.4's failure-kind taxonomy is itself verified. An implemented status depending on a planned prerequisite is legal, and the dependency is real — the aborted-versus-indeterminate discrimination this atom exists to make is a claim about that taxonomy — so the edge stays and the promotion waits on W6 rather than being eased by dropping it

items.summary: Advance C13-FACET-CONTRIBUTION-ATTRIBUTION from implemented with exact evidence
notes: Discharged: facet.slot-entry carries `package: PackagePin` as a declared field of the identity digest at codec major 3; an entry payload carrying no pin is refused and the major-2 bytes that used to carry one are refused as an unsupported major; the pinned entry restores through MemoryWorkspaceSlotStore and reopens through the SQLite Workspace slot store, both driven by the shared test/w3/slot-store-contract.ts seam contract. The installed Slot record was split from the manifest SlotDeclaration as facet.installed-slot so it carries attribution too, and derived Subscriptions carry it at workspace.subscription major 2, immutably across revisions

Discharged, and it was an absent mechanism rather than unwritten evidence: SPEC §4.2 requires that a slot hold at most one entry per contributor per ordinal so that a changed contribution supersedes its predecessor, and both stores refused the changed contribution instead. The entry id digests every declared field including the pin, so it answered `is this the same materialization` while being used as the supersession key, which is the two-questions-one-representation collapse; a Facet re-reading its contribution from a later release could therefore never re-materialize at the same position. src/facets/slot-entry.ts#SlotContributionOrigin now names the position as its own shape, WorkspaceSlotStore.contribute supersedes at an occupied origin inside one transaction, and WorkspaceSlotStore.requireFreeOrigin keeps the storage primitive from accreting behind it. The origin is derived from declared fields, so no record changed shape and no codec major moved: SlotEntry.toData() and every slot: identity digest are byte-identical across this change

One of the five unmaterialized kinds is now a record and four still are not, so the clause is partly discharged and the row stays at implemented. facet.surface-registration major 1 is src/facets/surface.ts#SurfaceRegistration: the manifest's SurfaceDescriptor plus a ContributionAttribution, the same declaration-plus-pin split facet.installed-slot makes, so the Surface id and title are not restated beside the descriptor and no second attribution model exists. It carries no registeredAt and no registration id — the SurfaceId is the position, and a wall-clock field would make re-materializing the same contribution from the same release a different record, which §4.2 forbids. The dead two-field `Surface` interface that duplicated the descriptor's id and title is gone. src/facets/surface-store.ts#WorkspaceSurfaceStore writes the registration and its attribution in one transaction, refuses a Surface another Facet registered, and computes its withdrawal set from attribution alone; src/facets/surface-memory.ts#MemoryWorkspaceSurfaceStore is the reference implementation and refuses a rewrite of stored bytes, so supersession is a retirement plus a fresh materialization rather than a write over an immutable record. Measured by mutation in this tree rather than inherited: 11 probes over 18 authored Surface cases, 10 discriminating, every kill an assertion failure. Dropping the attribution from the payload kills 13 cases and encoding a fixed contributor instead of the record's own kills 10; each half of the constructor's instanceof refusal kills exactly the missing-or-forged case; removing the absent-pin refusal in ContributionAttribution.decodeFields kills the Surface missing-or-forged-attribution case and the pre-existing source-pin naming case; dropping the contributor check kills exactly the another-Facet case, once at the seam and again at the storage primitive; ignoring attribution in the withdrawal set kills 3; dropping the same-record early return kills 2; superseding by rewrite instead of retirement kills 2. The one non-discriminating probe is an equivalent mutant and not a gap: making `package` optional in the registration's exact-field list changes nothing observable, because decodeFields still refuses the absent pin, which the probe above it measures. Still not discharged for the remaining four: no catalog entry, prompt section, ingress endpoint or merged settings fragment record exists, so for those there is nothing to attribute and no test that could fail if the MUST were violated. Each is its own slice and three of them land outside src/facets/, so they need the owning wave's own row — AGENTS.md forbids restoring the old OperationCatalog, prompt assembly is W5, ingress is W6 and settings fragments are W7. No substrate implementation of the Surface store exists yet, so seam discovery does not count it as a normative seam and that denominator is unchanged at 21

Discharged by the W0 rule this clause asked for, landed beside the row rather than by a W3 slice: artifacts/quality/rules.json registers ACQ-ATTRIBUTION at node architecture (21 rules at discharge; the clause measured 0 attribution-mentioning rules of its 19), scripts/quality/architecture.mjs asserts the atom, and artifacts/quality/gate-corpus.json proves the gate red instead of asserting it — its mutation deletes the PackagePin half from the ContributionAttribution refusal, and the building run measures that mutation turning architecture.mjs red with the pinned diagnostic while the unmutated control stays green (gate integrity: 27 mutations turned 21 of 21 rules red, 0 unproven). Citation discrimination, measured by mutation in an isolated worktree rather than inherited, and stated at the tier it was measured at. 16 probes; every clause of the rule that has a materialized record is defended, and every kill was an assertion failure rather than a collection error. Retiring the superseded predecessor and asking occupancy by position rather than by identity each kill 6 labelled cases; the per-contributor origin key kills exactly the supersedes-only-its-own case (1); a pin-gated supersession kills exactly the later-release case (2); dropping the same-entry early return kills exactly the idempotence case (2); neutering requireFreeOrigin kills exactly the occupied-origin case (2). items.summary: Advance C13-FACET-DEPENDENCY-ORDER from planned with exact evidence
notes: The declaration half exists and is already better keyed than a nominal string: src/facets/manifest.ts#BindingRequirement carries (name: BindingName, facet: FacetPackageId, compat: CompatRange) and round-trips through the facet manifest codec. items.summary: Advance C13-RUN-DISTINCTION-REPRESENTABLE from planned with exact evidence
notes: The merge half, in its discloser's own words. `RunCommit.parents` is a flat `readonly RunCommitId[]` with arity validated per kind, so `parents.length === 2` answers whether this has two entries while the rule needs whether this joins two distinct lineages. A merge naming ONE commit as both parents is fully constructable, passes the codec, and is refused only later by `RunRuntime.validateMerge` — a unary merge wearing binary shape. That is demonstrated rather than argued: dropping the runtime's distinctness clause survives every record-level check, so the record-level mutant is the one that lives. The absent mechanism is a `MergeParents` value object in src/agents/runs/commit.ts that cannot hold one commit twice, plus the codec path that admits only it

Stated honestly because the row must not read as a correctness gap: `RunRuntime.validateMerge` refuses the unary-merge case correctly today, and src/agents/runs/commit.ts refuses every arity but two. No wrong merge lands and no wrong answer is returned. This is a representability rule — the illegal value exists and is checked rather than being unconstructable — so the evidence owed is that the value cannot be built, never that a build is rejected

The omission-attribution half, in its discloser's own words. `TurnModelInput.covers` is per-RECORD, a flat `readonly RunCommitId[]`, while `TurnOmission` is per-SECTION, so the two facts sit at different granularities with no third field joining them. `covers` therefore answers whether a commit was in scope of the assembly while being read as whether the model observed that commit's content, and a host that lists a commit and renders zero bytes of it — fully abridging it inside a multi-commit section — is indistinguishable in the record from one that rendered it whole. The withheld byte count exists but cannot be attributed to a commit. The absent mechanism is a per-commit coverage entry in src/agents/runs/executor.ts

What the omission half does and does not break, from the same disclosure. Reconstruction stays byte-exact either way because the bytes come from the sections and not from the accounting, so C13-TURN-MODEL-INPUT-RECONSTRUCTABLE is unaffected, and C13-TURN-SURFACE-ACCOUNTED claims coverage equals the transcript and that abridgement states the withheld amount without claiming per-commit attribution, so no landed row overclaims and no test asserts something false. What is unavailable is the audit question of which commit was abridged — exactly the question a reader of the phrase compaction and abridgement compose would assume is answerable. It composes for reconstruction; it does not compose for attribution

Why it is owed rather than settled, in the discloser's own judgement: per-commit entries carrying carried versus withheld were considered and dropped as duplicative of the section-level omission, and that objection treated two different questions as one fact. Per-commit omission attribution is a fact about the world, so the duplication objection was wrong and the gap is debt rather than a decision

Replacing the field — `covers: readonly TurnCoveredCommit[]` with `{commit, omission}` per entry — changes the canonical value of an existing key, and `TurnModelInput.toData()` reaches `modelInputCommitId` through a content-addressed ref, so that shape forks every `modelInput` RunCommitId exactly as presence-typing `interceptable` forked InvocationIds, and it is a migration rather than a refactor. An ADDITIVE optional field emitted only when non-empty forks nothing: existing records serialise byte-identically and only records that use it differ, with `TurnShownContent.toData()` emitting `inline` XOR `ref` as the in-record precedent. Take the additive form; the residual cost is then §5.6 prose and one digest re-affirmation, not a durable-identity migration

Both halves are unmeasured against the mutation campaign, so no discrimination attribution exists for either mechanism. Discharging this row means the two value objects, a record-level test that a unary merge cannot be constructed rather than that it is rejected, a test that a fully abridged carried commit is distinguishable from a whole one, and the mutation attribution that shows each new test dies when its own clause is removed

Three p0 tests exercise exactly those three paths and none carries this atom's label, so no selector can be claimed until they are tagged. test/agents/runs/runtime-mutation.test.ts `append guards` > `rejects a parent commit that belongs to another Run` inserts a commit under RunId `run-elsewhere` and appends against it; `merge validation` > `merge requires an exact source branch and stored head commits` registers branch `branch-elsewhere` under RunId `run-elsewhere` and merges its head; `runtime lookup errors` > `effective commits reject a branch of another Run` covers the branch side. Moving this row to verified is the tagging plus ACQ-IMPORT and ACQ-TEST, not new behaviour

A positive assertion is owed alongside the rejections, because a runtime that rejected every merge would satisfy a rejection-only test: a merge whose source is a distinct branch of the same Run at equal pins is accepted, and the resulting graph still holds exactly one zero-parent commit. The second half is the interaction with C13-RUN-GRAPH-ARITY this rule depends on — closure and the single-root rule are one fact read from two directions — and no test asserts the zero-parent count after a merge
